families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer or blend hosts retain a plasticised acid/water network for cold-tolerant proton transport.
descriptor_match: D2: DES/plasticised polar domains are supported in chitosan blends and are favored for subambient continuity.
D3: starch/PVA and chitosan-based hosts are analogously flexible hydrogen-bonded films rather than rigid brittle matrices.
D6: starch, PVA, and acid-bearing blends provide dense donor/acceptor relay environments.
D7: chitosan and low-loaded phosphoric-acid strategies support retention of the conducting phase.

families.family_description: One-dimensional clay or nanotube hosts confine and retain phosphoric-acid-rich pathways while guiding percolation through a polymer matrix.
descriptor_match: D4: phosphoric acid or acid-complexed media are supported as mobile proton sources when confined or complexed.
D5: attapulgite and halloysite claims directly support interconnected nanoconfinement and channel guidance.
D7: attapulgite, halloysite, and chitosan support acid retention and reduced leaching.
D6: phosphoric-acid-containing composites provide proton-relay functionality.

families.family_description: Protonated phosphate networks offer amorphous retained proton media that can be hybridised with softer hosts for broader operating continuity.
descriptor_match: D1: phosphate glass directly supports an amorphous continuous proton-transport medium.
D6: phosphate networks provide strong hydrogen-bond-mediated proton mobility.
D7: phosphate media intrinsically retain the proton-conducting phase, though stability can be conditional.
D2: hybridisation with bound-water or plasticised hosts is an analogous route to improve cold-side continuity.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan-PVA blended film containing 1D attapulgite loaded or wetted with retained phosphoric acid.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-acid continuity in confined 1D channels
nanoconfinement: guided percolation through fibrous clay domains
retention: better acid hold-up than neat acid-doped polymer
risk_flags: PVA-specific low-temperature flexibility is analog rather than direct
PA loading may still need optimisation to avoid leaching
instances.novelty_rationale: The exact four-part combination is not directly claimed in the pool, but each role is individually supported. It is novel because it merges a film-forming OH-rich blend with a 1D acid-retaining clay route aimed at the cold window.

instances.composition_description: A starch-PVA host plasticised by a choline chloride/phosphoric acid deep-eutectic-like conducting phase.
expected_properties: cold_window: eutectic-like acid phase may suppress crystallisation on cooling
matrix: OH-rich blend should preserve hydrogen-bond connectivity
transport: mixed vehicular and relay proton motion is plausible
risk_flags: DES viscosity may become high near the cold end
acid-rich formulations may soften the film excessively
instances.novelty_rationale: This combines a starch/PVA hydrogen-bonded film with a ChCl/PA acid complexing motif not directly paired in the pool. The novelty lies in using the eutectic concept to target non-crystallising proton media in a low-temperature biopolymer film.

instances.composition_description: A starch-PVA membrane incorporating halloysite nanotubes as phosphoric-acid-confined proton-transport fillers.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: HNT lumen/surface interactions can retain acid domains
cold_window: bound acid in nanotubes may remain more mobile than bulk water
transport: starch/PVA OH network can bridge confined proton sites
risk_flags: interfacial compatibility between HNTs and blend may need surface tuning
PA overloading can still cause exudation
instances.novelty_rationale: The pool supports HNT-confined phosphoric acid and separately supports starch/PVA hydrogen-bond-rich hosts, but not this exact merger. It is novel because it substitutes fibrous nanotube confinement into a low-cost OH-rich blend for cold-side operation.

instances.composition_description: A quaternary-synergy membrane using chitosan-starch as biopolymer host, PVA as film former, 1D attapulgite as nanoconfiner, and retained phosphoric acid as proton source.
expected_properties: cold_window: bound-water and acid continuity are plausible across a plasticised OH-rich matrix
nanoconfinement: 1D clay should connect and retain acid-rich channels
mechanics: PVA can improve film integrity versus biopolymer/acid alone
risk_flags: multicomponent phase separation is possible without ratio control
acid retention remains sensitive to total hydration
instances.novelty_rationale: This is the requested quaternary synergy pattern, assembled from separately supported host, film-former, 1D clay, and acid roles. Its novelty is the deliberate co-location of multiple cold-favoring motifs in one membrane architecture.

instances.composition_description: An amorphous protonated phosphate glass used as a control retained-proton conductor without added polymer host.
expected_properties: pathway: direct amorphous proton-transport continuity is supported
retention: conducting species are intrinsically immobilised in the network
limitation: cold-side brittleness and dry-state transport may constrain practical membranes
risk_flags: conditional conductivity stability is noted in the literature
lack of plasticised bound-water phase may limit subambient performance
instances.novelty_rationale: This is retained as a control because the descriptor pool directly supports protonated phosphate glass as an amorphous proton reservoir. It provides a non-novel benchmark against which softer cold-oriented hybrids can be compared.
